readback.name: Poincare.MetricAdaptedLocalParametrix.exists_metric_adapted_local_parametrix
readback.mathematical_statement:
For every type M in universe u with a topology, Hausdorff (T2) and compactness instances, a charted-space instance modeled on real Euclidean three-space and a smooth manifold instance for the real identity model with corners at smooth-infinity exponent, for every supplied genuine smooth Riemannian metric g0 and every real alpha strictly between zero and one, there exist an actual AtlasData A and two families psi,xi of real spatial functions indexed by Fin A.cover.chartCount. AtlasData includes a finite extended-chart cover with anchors, open covering regions whose closures lie in the genuine chart sources and have compact coordinate images, and a smooth partition of unity subordinate to those regions. coordSupport A i is the coordinate image of the topological support of its partition function.
For every chart index i, psi i and xi i are smooth at smooth-infinity exponent and have compact support; each takes values in [0,1] everywhere. At every point of coordSupport A i, psi i equals one throughout some neighborhood (the eventually-at-nhds assertion). xi i equals one pointwise on tsupport(psi i); the type does not explicitly claim this equality is a germ on that whole support. tsupport(xi i) lies inside the actual chart target, and at every point of that support the fixed-anchor GeodesicTransport cutoff equals one on a neighborhood. Neither cutoff family nor A is a premise.
There also exist nonnegative real constants Cpsi,CP and a strictly positive common tau at most one, chosen before the lifespan T. For every real T with 0<T<=tau there exist families P and R of continuous real linear maps: P i maps the scalar parabolic Holder carrier Y(alpha,T) into Graph(alpha,T), and R i maps that Y into itself. These maps may depend on T. The Y carrier consists of bounded scalar functions on [0,T] times Euclidean three-space with the alpha Holder condition for the parabolic distance norm(spatial difference)+sqrt(abs(time difference)), represented as zero outside that cylinder. Graph stores u,ut,du,ddu in their respective Holder carriers, requires u at time zero to vanish, requires ordinary first and second spatial derivative identities on the cylinder, and requires the time derivative within [0,T]. It does not provide an ordinary time derivative across time zero or joint C3 regularity.
For each i, and unconditionally for every forcing f in Y and every space-time point p, if p spatial coordinate lies outside tsupport(psi i), then the u component of P i f is zero there. After that unconditional support assertion, the next three conclusions require the forcing-support premise that f p=0 for every p whose spatial coordinate lies outside coordSupport A i. Only for such supported f, at every space-time p the residual R i f p is chartValue(a,P i f,p)-f p, where a is the actual inverse Gram field of g0 in the chart anchored at A.cover.anchor i. chartValue is ut minus the sum over both Fin 3 indices of a times the spatial Hessian on canonical Euclidean basis vectors. Thus the residual sign is operator(P f)-f; the literal local relation is operator(P f)=f+R f. For the same supported f, ||R i f|| <= Cpsi*(T^((1-alpha)/2)+T^(1-alpha/2))*||f|| and ||P i f|| <= CP*||f||. The constants are common to every chart and every admissible T, but the displayed numerical norm estimates and residual identity are not asserted for arbitrary unsupported f. No spatial-support conclusion for R is explicitly included, and no unconditional operator-norm bound by these common constants is concluded.
There are no connectedness, simple-connectedness, second-countability, measurable-space, Borel, curvature, flow, positive-Einstein, or sphere-recognition premises. g0 is supplied rather than constructed. This produces scalar local operator families and buffers; it does not assert compatibility or symmetry across chart transitions, assembly into tensor-carrier operators, global right inversion, a Neumann correction, nonlinear Ricci or DeTurck flow, or a smooth limit. The empty-index case is allowed. No small-oscillation inequality is exported in this conclusion, although the residual bound uses the actual variable inverse-metric coefficients.
